title: Judge rejects Trump's bid to move his decided hush-money case to federal court
description_short: Judge rejects Trump's bid to move his decided hush-money case to federal court
description_medium: A federal judge rejected Trump's effort to move his already-decided New York hush-money criminal case into federal court. Reuters reported that the judge found the Supreme Court's presidential-immunity decision did not bear on this case. The ruling addressed removal after conviction and sentencing; it was not a new verdict on the underlying criminal charges.
description_long:
A federal judge denied Trump's request to move his New York criminal hush-money case into federal court after conviction and sentencing. Reuters reported the decision on August 28, 2026. The proceeding concerned an effort to change the court handling an already-decided case, rather than a new trial on the original allegations.

According to the supplied reporting, the judge found that the Supreme Court's presidential-immunity decision did not bear on this case. That finding addressed Trump's attempt to use the immunity ruling in support of removal. It should not be expanded into a claim that presidential immunity can never apply in any other proceeding.

The immediate result was rejection of this particular bid for a federal forum. The ruling did not itself constitute another conviction or a new sentencing decision. The supplied account also does not establish the eventual outcome of every other challenge Trump might pursue. The documented event is the failed removal effort and the judge's stated reason for rejecting it.

title: Judge orders press-pass restoration, finding Trump's ban likely denied due process
description_short: Judge orders press-pass restoration, finding Trump's ban likely denied due process
description_medium: Judge Timothy Kelly issued a 14-day temporary restraining order directing restoration of CNN, MS NOW and Politico credentials. The court found likely success on a due-process claim and questioned whether the asserted national-security rationale matched the record. The order provided temporary access relief while litigation continued, rather than a final ruling on every claim against the ban.
description_long:
Judge Timothy Kelly issued a 14-day temporary restraining order directing restoration of credentials for CNN, MS NOW and Politico. The supplied order found that the outlets were likely to succeed on their due-process claim and questioned whether the government's national-security explanation matched the record before the court.

Those findings explain the interim relief, but they are not the same as a final decision following full litigation. The court's assessment of likely success is part of the standard for granting temporary protection while the dispute proceeds. The government's asserted security rationale should likewise remain identified as its position, rather than treated as an established reason for excluding the outlets.

The immediate consequence was a direction to restore credentials for the specified period. The order did not, by itself, settle the scope of every future event, pool or grounds-access arrangement. The documented event is the temporary judicial intervention and its due-process basis, with compliance and longer-term relief remaining separate questions.

title: CNN and MS NOW reporters remain excluded from Xi arrival after press-pass order
description_short: CNN and MS NOW reporters remain excluded from Xi arrival after press-pass order
description_medium: CNN and MS NOW said their reporters were excluded from Xi Jinping's state-dinner arrival after a court ordered restoration of their White House hard passes. Other networks' reporters entered. AP reported eventual restoration of general grounds access, while pool and event restrictions continued. The episode distinguished possession of restored credentials from access to a particular presidential event.
description_long:
After a court ordered restoration of White House hard passes, CNN and MS NOW said their reporters were barred from the arrival for Xi Jinping's state dinner while reporters from other networks entered. The supplied AP account treats that exclusion as a subsequent access dispute, rather than another description of the initial credential ban.

AP also reported eventual restoration of general access to the White House grounds. That development did not eliminate every restriction: pool participation and access to individual events remained contested. The episode therefore involved different layers of press access that should not be collapsed into a single claim of complete restoration or complete exclusion.

The reporters' accounts of the arrival exclusion remain attributed to their outlets. The supplied reporting does not establish a final court finding about that particular incident. The supported event records the gap between the credential-restoration order and access to a specific presidential appearance, alongside the separate development involving general grounds access.
